transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um... hi. I guess I'm just having some trouble keeping track of things. Like... basic adult things. I keep forgetting to pay my bills, or... returning emails for job interviews. Missing appointments. Stuff like that. I just forget to follow through on errands, and... well, it's starting to actually cost me real opportunities. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Did you have similar trouble with attention or follow-through when you were a child?

Yeah, I guess so. Um... even back in elementary school, my teachers would always say I was smart, but... I don't know, they were always writing notes home. Like, about how I kept losing worksheets, or... just rushing through the instructions without really reading them. And I guess I talked out of turn a lot. My desk was always a disaster, too... like, so messy I could never find my homework when it was time to hand it in. So... yeah. It's been happening for a while.
Do you often feel physically restless, like you have trouble sitting still?

Yeah, I do. Um... it's hard to explain. Just... if I'm in an interview, or a meeting, or... even just trying to watch a movie, I get this... pressure. Like inside. It just builds up, and I feel like I have to move, or shift around, or... do something with my hands. If I can't, it just feels like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. So... yeah. Sitting still is hard.
Do you remember having these attention or forgetfulness problems before age 12?
Yeah... I mean, I think so. Like I said, the teachers were always writing notes home in elementary school. So... yeah, definitely before I was 12.
Do you also tend to act before thinking, like blurting things out or interrupting people?

Um... yeah, sometimes. I guess... if I'm talking to someone, or... like in an interview... I tend to just jump in before they're done. I usually think I know where they're going with it, so... I just start talking. But then I realize I cut them off... or I end up answering the wrong question entirely. So... yeah.
Do these attention and follow-through problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work or school and at home?
Um... I don't really know. I'm not working right now, so... I guess I mostly just notice it at home. I haven't really kept track of where it happens, to be honest.
